raw_response:
Alright, let me think through this year. I'm sitting with my tea in the morning, the wheat is already jointing out there, and I need to plan the rest.

---

**My thinking, as me:**

I've got 6.5 mu total. The way I split it: 4.5 mu goes to the wheat-maize double crop — that's my food security, my bedrock. The other 2 mu I put to chili, because chili brings cash. Without the chili money I can't pay for my grandson's school things and the daughter-in-law's medicines. My wife and I do most of the field work; the son works construction in Handan most of the year and the daughter-in-law helps at picking time.

*Wheat (already in the ground since last October on 4.5 mu):*
I planted Jimai 22 again like the last few years — the seed shop in town has it and my neighbor Old Wang gets good yields with it. Before planting I put down about 40 kg per mu of the 15-15-15 compound, that's what the agricultural station guy recommends for our soil here. Now it's late April, the wheat is jointing. I already did the pre-winter irrigation in November and the returning-green irrigation last month. Next month around jointing I'll topdress about 10 kg urea per mu and irrigate again. Then one more irrigation at grain filling if it doesn't rain. Three irrigations total usually, maybe four if it's dry. Last year I got about 440 kg/mu, this year looks similar — the stand is decent.

*Maize (goes in right after wheat, mid-June, same 4.5 mu):*
Zhengdan 958 hybrid, same as always. The window between wheat harvest and maize planting is tight — maybe five days. I use the small two-wheel tractor with the seeder attachment, my cousin's, I pay him in grain. No tilling, just direct seed into the stubble. Base fertilizer about 30 kg of compound per mu with the seeder, then topdress 10-12 kg urea at the big trumpet stage. One irrigation usually, maybe two if July is dry. Yield around 500 kg/mu, sometimes better.

*Chili (2 mu, transplanting starts now, end of April):*
This is the hard one, takes most of our labor. I bought seedlings from the nursery in the neighboring village — 120 yuan per mu worth. Transplant end of April. Chili needs more fertilizer than grain — I put base fertilizer around 50 kg compound per mu, then topdress twice with urea and potash. I irrigate maybe 5-6 times through the summer, the well is close but electricity for pumping adds up. Pests are a real problem — aphids, thrips, and the virus disease they bring. I spray four, five times through the season. The wife and daughter-in-law help with picking from July through September. Prices jumped last year to nearly 8 yuan/kg fresh at peak, so I'm hoping for that again, but you never know with chili.

I keep about 2,000 yuan cash aside for emergencies. Total input spending this year will be around 5,500-6,000 yuan. Tight but manageable. I won't push the fertilizer higher than usual — fertilizer prices are still high and I don't want to gamble.
